Research/2025-26/Exoplanets

Exoplanets

Analyzing VLTI/GRAVITY Data of Beta Pictoris b for Exomoon-Induced Exoplanetary Wobble

A search for an exomoon signal in the tiny astrometric motion of a directly imaged exoplanet.

Research question

What did the project ask?

Can an exomoon around Beta Pictoris b be detected through the small astrometric wobble it would induce in the planet's motion?

Significance

Why does it matter?

A confirmed exomoon would illuminate satellite and planetary-system formation while extending moon searches beyond transit surveys.

Method

What did the team do?

The team reduced VLTI/GRAVITY interferometric observations with EsoRex and ExoGravity, fitted a two-planet Keplerian baseline with orbitize!, and examined the remaining astrometric residuals for a moon-induced signal.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

No exomoon was detected. Residuals remained at the scale of tens of milliarcseconds, well above an expected signal of tens to hundreds of microarcseconds, because the short observational baseline did not constrain the planetary orbit closely enough.
